About

I'm a second-year M.Tech student in Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Patna and a Junior Researcher in its Cybersecurity Lab, where I work with Dr. Somnath Tripathy.

Most of my work comes back to one question: what happens when a system's trust assumptions meet an adversary who doesn't share them? I first asked it of ARP, then of LLM-generated code, and now of cross-chain bridges, which fail when verifiers, signers or relayers stop behaving the way the security argument assumes. I'm working on AI agents that detect and explain these failures, and I built Crucible, a testbed that replays historical bridge exploits on forked chains, so that this work can be tested against real attacks.

I also study the other side of AI in security: how attackers use LLMs, and how far LLM judgments about code and smart contracts can be trusted.

Research interests

  • Cross-chain & blockchain security
  • Agentic AI for security
  • Adversarial uses of LLMs
  • Reliability of LLMs in security analysis
  • Network & protocol security
  • Trust assumptions in distributed systems

Research software

  • Crucible Code in limited access

    A CLI-first, modular testbed for EVM bridge security research. It forks chains at historical blocks and reruns exploits deterministically, with structured run artifacts and a plugin SDK for attack, bridge and LLM-agent plugins. Ships with benchmark reproductions of the Wormhole, Nomad, Poly Network, Horizon, BNB Bridge and Multichain incidents.

    Python, Foundry, Solidity, DockerDocs

  • Private Ethereum Research Testbed

    A multi-node proof-of-work Ethereum network on lab machines at IIT Patna, with a faucet and a role-based dashboard, used for smart-contract security experiments and academic projects.

    Geth, Docker, Flask, Nginx

  • CryptoSIM

    A desktop application for teaching cryptography and blockchain through interactive simulation: 310 primitives and an instructor-facing Professor Mode.

    Rust, TauriSite
